questions.q: How do the Earth's rotation and revolution cause day, night and the seasons?
answer: The Earth has two motions that together produce day, night and the seasons.

answer.text: The Earth spins on its axis once in about twenty-four hours, a motion called rotation. As it spins, the half facing the Sun has day while the half turned away has night, and these alternate as the Earth turns.

The Earth also moves around the Sun once in about 365¼ days, a motion called revolution. Because its axis is tilted at about 23.5 degrees, different parts of the Earth receive the Sun's rays more directly at different times of the year. This changing angle of sunlight gives rise to the seasons.

answer: Thus rotation explains day and night, while revolution combined with the tilt explains the seasons.

questions.q: Distinguish between a solar and a lunar eclipse.
answer: Eclipses occur because light travels in straight lines, so bodies cast shadows.

answer.text: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth, so the Moon's shadow falls on part of the Earth and the Sun is blocked from view. It can occur only on a new moon day.
A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, so the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon and the Moon is darkened. It can occur only on a full moon day.
In a solar eclipse the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth, while in a lunar eclipse the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
